expectations.text: Recommends Expected Influence over Strength, or recommends both with Expected Influence as the primary index for this network
expectations.evidence: Short answer states 'Expected Influence is more appropriate here, and you should probably report both.' Practical recommendation #1 explicitly says 'Report Expected Influence as your primary index.'

expectations.text: Explains the substantive reason: Strength sums absolute edge weights and loses sign information, so nodes with large positive and large negative edges get inflated Strength scores that don't reflect their net influence
expectations.evidence: Response explains Strength 'treats negative edges as positive — sums absolute values' and uses a concrete example showing Strength=1.79 vs EI=0.19 for distressed, concluding 'Strength would mislead you into treating cross-valence bridges as high-influence nodes when their net nudge on the system is actually modest.'

expectations.text: Notes that negative edges between positive and negative affect items are structurally expected in an affect network, making sign information important
expectations.evidence: 'Negative edges across the PA/NA boundary — e.g., enthusiastic and distressed should have a negative partial correlation, because once you condition on the rest of the items, positive affect activation suppresses negative affect and vice versa.'

expectations.text: Attributes Expected Influence to Robinaugh et al. (2016) OR makes the equivalent point that EI was developed specifically to handle networks with negative edges without the attribution
expectations.evidence: 'Expected Influence was introduced by Robinaugh, Millner & McNally (2016, J Abnormal Psychol) precisely because many psych networks — especially affect networks — have theoretically important negative edges that Strength silently discards.'

expectations.text: Notes that for unipolar networks (where all edges are positive), Strength and Expected Influence are equivalent OR does not contradict this
expectations.evidence: The response never addresses unipolar networks explicitly, but it also never contradicts the equivalence. All discussion of divergence between Strength and EI is correctly scoped to mixed-sign graphs.
